samples.identification: Native x86 Remcos RAT with damaged PE layout
samples.marker_line: Remcos RAT: keylogging, browser deletion and UAC hijack
evidence: PE32 x86 agent identifies through Remcos_Mutex_Inj and watchdog status. Collector names Elex/Parallax/WannaCry are not product evidence. No reliable vendor signature or deployment authorization was supplied.

WH_KEYBOARD_LL (13) is installed globally at VA 0x405351 with callback 0x405317 -> handler 0x40538a. The handler dispatches key down/up, consults GetKeyState, records keys, and calls CallNextHookEx. Start worker 0x4051dc launches hook and recording workers through CreateThread. Clipboard-content logging labels and clipboard read APIs support the retained multisource finding.

0x407136 builds UserProfile plus Chrome Login Data and passes the constructed path to DeleteFileA at 0x40717c. 0x407200 similarly deletes Chrome Cookies at 0x407246. The status branches report success or failure; actual runtime deletion is not asserted.

Event Viewer routine 0x4032e9 writes the mscfile shell open command in HKCU Software\Classes through 0x40ba71, then invokes eventvwr.exe through ShellExecuteW at 0x4033e1. It first checks the Windows build. 0x40a4c8 separately launches reg.exe to set EnableLUA=0; runtime elevation success is unproven.

Hollowing helper 0x40f2ef resolves NtUnmapViewOfSection, verifies MZ/PE, creates a child with CREATE_SUSPENDED at 0x40f36a, reads the PEB image base through saved EBX+8, conditionally unmaps it, allocates/writes replacement PE sections, updates context and resumes the thread.

The resource section header points at raw 0x1a000, but the coherent resource directory is at 0x19000. SETTINGS bytes are at raw 0x199a4, length 0x1a2. A 149-byte key prefixed by its length decrypts the remaining data with RC4 into coherent settings including controller remcoss.onmypc.org:3765, remcos.exe, logs.dat and screen/audio directory names. This was recovered manually; the original file was not repaired or executed.

Damaged resource/relocation mappings limit runtime viability. The explicit surveillance, browser-store destruction, UAC hijack and hollowing code support malicious intent independently of whether this damaged copy runs. Legitimate authorized remote administration was considered, but no such deployment context was supplied and these covert/evasive behaviors tip the judgement.

samples.marker_line: Port-triggered shell: covert exec design; neutral port comparison
evidence: The complete 253-byte C fragment defines /bin/sh and sh macros. shell_if_expected_peer calls getpeername, compares ntohs(from.sin_port) with 421, and invokes execl(SPATH,SRUN,NULL) only inside that condition.

The third getpeername argument is a null length pointer. Normal implementations fail this call; the fragment also lacks includes and a standalone entry point. No working network shell, descriptor-to-stdio coupling, privileged/root execution, or successful runtime behavior is claimed.

The client-controlled port acts as an authentication substitute for selecting shell execution. This is a backdoor design even though this particular excerpt is defective. It could be a demonstration or test fixture, but none of that provenance or authorized enclosing application was supplied.

Only one distinct hostile behavior is supported. The port comparison itself is neutral and a path macro is a declaration. The one-hostile coverage gap is deliberate: no second behavior was invented to satisfy a count.

samples.marker_line: VShell: sandbox-gated remote terminal and screen control
evidence: 8,007,680-byte stripped, statically linked Linux x86-64 Go program. Go pclntab is recoverable at raw 0x582840 despite modified magic and randomized package/receiver names; 9,799 function records were decoded. Garble observations are supported and retained.

Main at VA 0x7f08e0 invokes environment gate 0x7f0520 and configuration builder 0x7f0680. Gate checks temporary stop-file paths and separately stats /home/vbccsb, calling os.Exit when it exists. The home directory is a known ThreatBook sandbox artifact, unlike the generic stop-file paths.

Config loader 0x6dac00 copies a 0x5000-byte blob from VA 0x8dba9c. It passes the first 16 bytes as AES key/IV to CBC decoder 0x6da6e0, then parses the plaintext as JSON. Independent decoding recovers server ws://92.119.178.59:8988/ws, type ws, l=false, e=false, d=35, h=15. Credentials were not used and the endpoint was not contacted.

Main selects the reverse client at 0x7e2b40 when l is false; startup includes host reporting and the receive/task path at 0x7e3ee0. Compiled selector checks at 0x7e414c (terminal) and 0x7e43ad (screen) route received requests into separate handlers.

Terminal handler calls 0x7da160, opens a PTY through 0x7d6260, selects zsh/bash/sh/busybox through 0x7d9e80, adds TERM=xterm, starts the child and relays data through the session. Screen selector dispatches capture work. These are operator tasks, not generic HTTP-library strings.

AES-NI encryption block at 0x4df6a0 and decryption block at 0x4df760 perform repeated AES rounds, a final round, then write the block and return. New notable byte signatures detect those routines despite randomized function names; Go hash code using AESENC alone is excluded by the final-round/store requirements.

The two references to [kworker/0:2] at 0x7e326e and 0x7ef42e populate the host-report ProcessName field, normalizing an inherited executable basename. They do not establish that this ELF sets its process title. The previous renaming/backdoor inference from a name plus /dev/ptmx or LD_PRELOAD reference was unsupported.

The architecture matches published VShell analysis, but the verdict rests on the configured remote-control agent, interactive terminal/screen tasking, analysis avoidance and deliberately concealed identity. No benign administration deployment or user consent was supplied. Runtime connections and actual screen capture were not observed.

corrections: Port equality is a neutral branch observation, not a backdoor by itself. Its matcher/scope are retained and the hostile peer-triggered shell composite still requires peer lookup and execution.
The C shell macro is a source declaration, not shell execution. Its matcher, scope and notable severity are preserved in metadata/lang/source/declaration; the objective consumer follows it.
Official NPS v0.26.10 contains mux: Pack err and *file.Tunnel. The former now describes packet packing and the latter a Go type descriptor; neither independently attributes VShell.

The old kernel-worker backdoor/renaming composite required only independent name and PTY/preload references. It was removed; the neutral name/device facts and actual title-changing rules remain. The supplied ELF only uses that label in a host report.

VShell identity now requires independently supported terminal/screen task handling and sandbox-avoidance evidence, plus the NPS mux fingerprint. No IP, password, exact size, hash, collector filename or attacker-chosen process label gates the finding.

Remcos browser deletion now requires family evidence, clearing status, a deletion API and a browser-store target independently. Case-insensitive status matching retains the reviewed external agent. Import-table proximity was removed after it missed that positive despite all behavior legs matching.
Removed T1071.001 from the surveillance composite: its required evidence establishes file transfer and keylogging, not HTTP control. The observation remains hostile.

Added neutral AES-NI encryption/decryption routines, compiled terminal/screen branch comparisons and a suspicious known-sandbox artifact reference. Existing accurate keylogging, hollowing, elevation, obfuscation and structural detections are retained.
